summary.headline: The Regional School Committee approved a $31.4 million FY27 budget, applied $675,000 from reserves, and adopted the 2026-2027 Option 5 calendar.
summary.summary: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee voted to approve a recommended FY27 operating budget of $31,416,287, reflecting a 5.81 percent increase driven primarily by out-of-district special education and health insurance costs. To reduce the impact on member towns, the committee approved using $675,000 in Excess and Deficiency reserves, bringing Southborough's assessment increase to 4.83 percent for operations. The committee also reconsidered and approved the 2026-2027 school calendar Option 5, accepted a $50,000 state grant for student support regulations, and approved eight new high school courses.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved open meeting minutes from January 21, 2026, Operational Budget Subcommittee minutes from February 3, 2026, and executive session minutes from January 21, 2026. Later in the meeting, members reviewed an empty monthly personnel report and noted the distribution of the complete FY27 budget book before adjourning at 9:03 p.m.
key_details: Open and subcommittee minutes approved by roll call.
Monthly personnel report had no new items.
FY27 budget books distributed to committee members.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved; meeting adjourned at 9:03 p.m.

topics.title: Algonquin Athletic Boosters Club presentation
topics.summary: The president of the Algonquin Athletic Boosters Club presented an overview of the organization's structure, financial status, and partnership with the athletic department. The Boosters operate as an independent 501(c)(3) entity providing equipment, apparel, banquets, and facility support across all high school sports.
key_details: From July 2023 to January 2026, total Booster revenues were $596,000 against expenses of $550,000.
All 28 team booster sub-accounts maintain positive balances.
The Boosters implemented seasonal meetings with parent sport representatives and strict review on any expenditure over $500.
The organization is reviewing lines between school-funded athletic expenses and booster supplemental spending.
topics.outcome: Information presented; committee thanked booster volunteers.

topics.title: Legislative and state budget update
topics.summary: District administrators reported on ongoing state budget developments and advocacy efforts regarding escalating special education transportation costs. The committee also noted the upcoming statewide school committee advocacy event.
key_details: District is monitoring the state legislature as House budget numbers are expected shortly.
Administrators highlighted a recent Boston Globe article detailing how special education transportation funding formulas are failing school districts.
The annual Day on the Hill legislative event is scheduled for March 30, 2026.

topics.title: Multilingual learner education annual report
topics.summary: The director of multilingual learners delivered the annual department report detailing enrollment trends, state regulatory updates, and instructional support. The district currently supports students across 13 home languages using a Sheltered English Immersion model.
key_details: Algonquin currently serves 57 multilingual students, comprising 25 active English Learners and 32 Former English Learners.
15 English Learners are newly enrolled in the district this academic year.
Top native languages spoken are Portuguese (38 percent), Spanish (17.5 percent), and Arabic (5.2 percent).
100 percent of students participated in 2025 ACCESS testing, with 61.5 percent achieving state progress targets.
Upcoming International Night is scheduled for May 1, 2026, in the high school library.

topics.title: State grant for timeout practice regulations
topics.summary: Administrators presented a $50,000 state grant from the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education to align district practices with new state regulations taking effect in June 2025 regarding student timeout spaces.
key_details: Grant provides $50,000 from DESE.
Funds will support professional development, restorative practices, and tiered behavioral interventions.
Goal is to reduce student seclusion and foster inclusive learning environments.
topics.outcome: Committee voted 6-0 to accept the $50,000 grant.

topics.title: Student advisory and high school principal reports
topics.summary: The student advisory representative and high school principal reported on student life, a multi-year substance use prevention partnership with Encompass, and approved course changes. The high school is adding eight new courses under updated graduation requirements.
key_details: Student Advisory Committee is conducting a mental health survey and working with cafeteria staff on expanded vegetarian/vegan options.
Encompass partnership provides opioid awareness and Narcan training for grade 11, substance abuse lessons for grade 10, adulting 101 for seniors, and grade 9 orientation.
The high school and Encompass will host a professional development session on March 23, 2026, with the Boston University School of Public Health to analyze female adolescent health data.
Eight new courses approved for the Program of Studies include AP Business and Personal Finance, Data and Decision-Making, and Working with Children.
The new graduation requirements add a fourth year of math, expand fine/performing arts to a full year, and add two years of world language.

topics.title: FY26 budget transfers and revenue report
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and approved line item transfers and financial reports through January 31, 2026. The general operational budget maintained a surplus of just under $400,000, while building maintenance ran over budget due to winter cold snap repairs to rooftop HVAC units.
key_details: General fund budget balance as of January 31 was $397,000, or 1.34 percent of the budget.
Building maintenance was over budget due to severe cold-weather repairs on rooftop heating units.
District received its first regional transportation installment of $449,689 from the state and $6,100 in Medicaid reimbursements.
The district froze non-essential operational spending to protect reserves for FY27.
topics.outcome: Committee approved the FY26 line item transfers, expenditure report, and statement of revenue in two unanimous 6-0 votes.

topics.title: FY27 recommended operating and capital budget
topics.summary: The superintendent and finance director presented the final recommended FY27 operating budget of $31,416,287, representing a 5.81 percent increase over FY26. Over 59 percent of the increase is driven by out-of-district special education tuitions, special education transportation, and a 9.99 percent rise in health insurance costs.
key_details: Total FY27 operating budget is $31,416,287, an increase of $2,071,974 (5.81 percent).
Reductions from initial 12.79 percent requests totaled over $2 million, including cutting 5.5 FTE staff positions primarily through attrition and applying $724,353 in FY26 Circuit Breaker funds.
Capital assessment totals $477,000, apportioned as $292,210 for Northborough (61.26 percent) and $184,790 for Southborough (38.74 percent).
Committee approved applying $675,000 from Excess and Deficiency (E&D) reserves to offset town assessments.

With $675,000 in E&D applied, Southborough's operating assessment increases by 4.83 percent ($458,249) to $9,943,542, and its total assessment including debt and capital increases by 6.58 percent ($663,101) to $10,733,409.
topics.outcome: Committee voted 6-0 to approve the FY27 budget, 6-0 to apply $675,000 in E&D reserves, and 6-0 to approve the $477,000 capital assessment.
topics.why_it_matters: Sets the regional high school budget and the property tax assessment formulas heading to Annual Town Meeting in Southborough and Northborough.

topics.title: 2026-2027 school calendar reconsideration
topics.summary: The committee reconsidered its December 2025 vote on the 2026-2027 academic calendar to align regional high school operations with the member towns. Members debated calendar Option 5, which removes staff professional development days from Yom Kippur and Eid and places a professional development day on Orthodox Good Friday.
key_details: Teachers report on August 27, 28, and 31, 2026, for three consecutive professional development days.
First day of school for students will be September 1, 2026, and the scheduled last day is June 17, 2027 (without snow days).
Option 5 removes professional development days from Yom Kippur (Sept 21) and Eid (March 10), and adds a professional development day on Orthodox Good Friday (April 30).
Southborough previously voted for Option 5; Northborough is scheduled to vote on Option 5 in March.
The motion carried 4-1-1, with one member voting no in objection to selecting specific religious holidays and one member abstaining.
topics.outcome: Committee voted 4-1-1 to adopt calendar Option 5 for the 2026-2027 school year.
topics.why_it_matters: Determines the start and end dates and holiday closures for all regional high school students and aligns schedules across the regional district.

topics.title: Policy updates: Competency determination and class standing
topics.summary: The committee conducted second readings on two high school policies, voting to adopt a new state-mandated competency determination policy and repealing an obsolete class standing policy.
key_details: Adopted new Competency Determination Policy J-400 following approval from the state.
Rescinded Class Standing Policy J-190 because credit-based standing definitions are obsolete under updated student handbook graduation standards.
topics.outcome: Policy J-400 approved 6-0; Policy J-190 rescinded 6-0.

votes.motion: Approve the acceptance of the DESE grant for implementing updated timeout regulations in the amount of $50,000
Approve the FY26 budget line item transfers and the monthly General Fund expenditure report as of January 31, 2026
Approve the Statement of Revenue report as of January 31, 2026
Approve the recommended FY27 operating budget of $31,416,287, representing an increase of 5.81 percent over FY26
Approve the transfer of $675,000 from the Excess and Deficiency (E&D) account to apply to the FY27 operational budget
Approve the FY27 capital assessment of $477,000
Reconsider the vote of December 3, 2025, and approve 2026-2027 school calendar Option 5
Approve new Competency Determination Policy J-400 on second reading

public_comment.summary: A resident and educator urged the committee not to adopt calendar Option 5, arguing that public school calendars should recognize only federal holidays paired with robust religious accommodation policies to treat all faith backgrounds equitably without disrupting educational continuity.

A resident spoke in support of approving calendar Option 5, commending the superintendent and teachers' associations for collaborative work to maintain calendar consistency across the regional district.
